item.description:
Code-file changes read as a diff, a change waiting off screen keeps its mark at the window's edge, and writer badges count only what is left to review.
- List bullets move with their lines, a period after inline code stays on the code's line, struck text sits flush or hangs when it would push its line, and a rewrite across lines hangs its old text as one block. - Code-file changes read as a diff (old lines above, − and + with numbers in the gutter) with Revert and Keep on the stamp and a build error on it; every stamp shows Keep filled and its keys, sized from the body text; a revert leaves "Reverted · ⌘Z" in the margin; a named writer's insert drops the solid underline unless Differentiate Without Color or Increase Contrast is on. - The first-run demo says the stamp reads CLAUDE CODE, as it does, and Settings > Appearance says inline code is 0.9 of the text while code blocks match the x-height. - First run and setup: the guide points at the stamp's Revert button, Skip and Done read as buttons, the status bar keeps its height once shown, and Set Up Agent Hooks… opens one sheet that leads with what hooks send and names the events. A folder's empty page leads with Copy a Test Prompt, and File > Open… takes a folder. - Earlier Versions names the agent on every version one of its turns wrote, not only the last, when two writes land within a second. - Earlier Versions shows each change with two lines around it, word by word in the writer's color, says under each row what it changed ("+12 words · Backoff"), folds an agent's turn into one row, shows a pin only where it applies, and fits a 620 pt window. Mermaid labels use the text font in 6 pt boxes, H1 tracking loosens to -0.01 em, and images take a 1 px edge in both themes (12% dimmer in dark). - A change waiting off screen keeps its mark at the window's right edge at rest, and one that lands there pins a chip ("1 more below · Backoff ⌃⌘↓") until it is on screen or decided. - Writer badges count only changes waiting for Keep or Revert, so they add up to "N to review", and say "1 change by Claude Code, not reviewed"; untracked files read New; the review menu heads each writer with its ink and count; the status bar says "Next change: spec.md ⌃⌘↓". Quick Open shows its prefixes, a magnifier and a stronger selection; Find in Files rows wrap to two lines, carry the badge and git letter, and use symbol toggles and the system find highlight.

Review keys follow one rule, agent changes are marked with the writer's color instead of a letter, and marks stay on their words while you type above them.
- Review keys follow one rule: Return keeps and Delete reverts; ⌘ acts on one change, Shift on the note, Control on the session. Keep Session moves to ⌃⌘↩, beside Revert Session (⌃⌘⌫) (decision 0013). Quick Open moves to ⌘P and Print to ⌥⌘P; ⇧⌘O no longer opens Quick Open. - Typing above a marked change keeps its marks on their words. A short note opened while its window is behind draws all its text. A Mermaid chain with a labeled link (`a -->|x| b --> c`) draws every edge. - ⇧⌘R puts the keyboard in the Changes list on its first change, so J and K no longer type into the note. A stamp's count matches the toolbar's "N to review": git's uncommitted changes no longer add to it. - Change stamps say Claude Code in full. Revert and Keep are small native buttons with their keys in the tooltip and VoiceOver's help, and stay visible on a folded stamp. A revert says "Reverted · ⌘Z to undo" for 4 s. Another app's and the demo's changes take a plum hue, removed text reads at 58% ink, and the column no longer slides when the rail appears. - Writer badges on sidebar rows and tabs are a dot in the writer's ink and the count, instead of a letter that read as git's (A, C, D, M, R); the name is in the tooltip and VoiceOver. - Earlier Versions lists one write as one row: the version it replaced keeps the time it was written, and browsing adds no copy of the current text. A wrapped diff line hangs past the + and − gutter, and the diff scrolls to its first difference. - A note opens with the caret past its first-line H1 or front matter, not at its end; a restored tab and Back and Forward still return to where you were. - Tables and code blocks wider than the line width run on to 32 points from the window's right edge instead of wrapping early; prose stays at the line width. - The hook offer comes once you keep or revert the first change another app makes in an open note, not when a folder opens, and names each settings file it edits and whether it reaches every project. - Code files always open, and the sidebar, Quick Open and Find in Files list them; Settings > Editor drops Open code files. - Settings > Agents says whether the `dewline` command is installed, and where, with Add when it isn't. The Settings window fits each pane. - First run: Welcome.md is two sentences above the demo, the guide clears the note and ends on Open a Folder…, and the test prompt targets a new dewline-test.md and prints under its button. - Long tab names keep their extension, Find in Files has a labeled Replace toggle and one-line results, Quick Open marks code files, and app buttons are standard macOS push buttons. - The status bar shows a hint such as "Next: spec.md ⌃⌘↓" beside the caret's place instead of over it, and drops it once the caret moves or a change lands. - Dark-mode images draw at 85% brightness, inline code at 0.9 of the text size, and wrapped task items start under their label.

View > Changes no longer crashes, code files and Source mode show their text again, and the first launch walks you through a real agent change.
- View > Changes no longer crashes when it lists a session. - Code files, Typst and LaTeX files, and Source mode show their text again; the line-number gutter had painted over it. - Run from the disk image or Downloads, Dewline offers to move itself to Applications before anything else, since a copy there loses its updates and hooks once the image ejects. - The first launch runs a short guide in Welcome.md: a demo agent edits the note, you revert one change and keep the other, then a setup list offers a folder, the Markdown handler, agent hooks and the `dewline` command, each skippable. A second launch skips it. - Adding the `dewline` command refuses a copy on a disk image or a translocated path and offers the move instead. - The disk image opens to a laid-out window: Dewline on the left, Applications on the right, in light and dark.

Agent edits are easier to review from the keyboard and across a whole folder, uncommitted git changes show as marks, the window behaves more like a Mac app, and Typst and LaTeX files typeset in a sandbox.
- A file deleted since the last commit stays in the sidebar as a struck-through row; clicking it opens the Changes pane. - The sidebar's folder header shows how many files changed since the last commit and how many commits the branch is ahead of its upstream ("main ↑2 · 7 changed"); Activity carries the same line while the sidebar is collapsed. Changed files' context menus add Review Uncommitted Changes. - Filled chrome buttons use the theme accent with paper text. - Under Full Keyboard Access, chrome buttons, the folder pop-up and the tab strip take the focus with the system's focus ring and act on Space or Return; the arrow keys move between tabs. A list that has the keyboard shows its selection as a solid accent pill. - Find in Files results use the theme's inks. - Dragging a tab slides its neighbors aside as it passes; dragging it out of the strip drags the note's file. The unsaved dot sits where the close button appears on hover, Command-click on a tab shows the note's path, and the tab's tooltip names its Option-Command key. - Chrome type follows the macOS text styles; chevrons and the tab close button are SF Symbols. Activity and the sidebar's … menu open on mouse down, and Activity dims instead of hiding while you type. Command-Down Arrow opens the selected sidebar row. - Set Up Agent Hooks refuses to run from a disk image or a translocated copy, whose path is gone once it ejects, and offers Move to Applications and Relaunch; the first launch offers the move too, and `dewline doctor --install-hooks` refuses the same paths. - The hook setup sheet lists every event it adds for each agent and what each group is for, says the hooks apply in every project (your user settings), and that they send paths and hashes, never file content. - Welcome.md puts "Show me a change" above the explanation, in the accent with a full underline, a pointing hand and the tip "Click to see a change"; its "Settings > Agents" opens the hook setup sheet. - The first agent change in a session says in the status bar: "First change from Claude Code. Keep or Revert it here." - The launch window shows the brand lockup, says "Open the folder your agent works in. Its edits show up marked, ready to keep or revert." when it lists nothing, and Return opens the selected recent instead of making a new note (⌘N still does). - The demo's writer is "Demo agent" on its stamp and in Earlier Versions, and its paragraph says the stamp reads CLAUDE, CODEX or CURSOR once hooks are set up. - Earlier Versions tints restored and removed lines in the theme's colors. - The window goes as narrow as 420 pt with the sidebar and Changes pane closed, so it shares a laptop screen with a terminal; below 700 pt the sidebar collapses on its own and comes back when the window widens. The Changes pane can narrow to 260 pt. - Changes (⇧⌘R) takes the keyboard on the first change; pressed again it hands the keyboard back to the note. In the list, J and K move, Y or Return keeps, X reverts, O reveals. Vim's ]c and [c are Next and Previous Change, and the command palette finds Changes by "Diff" or "Review". - Next Change (⌃⌘↓) past the last change in the open notes opens the next note waiting, changed while closed or since the last commit, at its first change, and the status bar says how many more wait. - The folder page lists notes deleted since the last commit; opening one shows its committed text, read-only. - With agent hooks on, the folder page offers Copy a Test Prompt to make the first marked change. - Keep on the change stamp and Keep Yours on the conflict card fill with the theme's accent instead of the system accent. - Changes rows show a change over several lines as "+N / −M lines" and open it in full with → or Space; note headings show the path in the folder, session names are small section labels, and changed words take the writer's ink instead of bold. - The change stamp reads "CLAUDE 3:25 PM · saved · 1 of 2", shows Next Change's keys only under the pointer or once you've decided a change, draws its shortcuts as keycaps, and its tooltips read "Option-click: Keep All (⇧⌘↩)". - The status bar keeps its line in a folder window so messages no longer move the note, reads results and problems to VoiceOver, and shows a problem ahead of a request. - Revert on a change you typed inside asks first, showing what it puts back, instead of refusing. - Code blocks highlight in a fixed band against the paper, keywords in the accent's hue, so tokens read apart from the text in light and dark themes. - Headings step by 1.25 from the body: 31, 25, 20 and 16 pt at the default size, so H3 no longer matches body text. - Edit has Paste and Match Style (⌥⇧⌘V), Delete, and Spelling and Grammar, Substitutions and Transformations submenus; Find has Find and Replace… (⌥⌘F), Use Selection for Find (⌘E) and Jump to Selection (⌘J); File > Duplicate takes ⇧⌘S. Smart Punctuation moves into Edit > Substitutions. - Go to Line… (⌘L) opens Quick Open on its line scope instead of a dialog. - Settings > Appearance sets line height on a slider from 1.3 to 1.6. - Writers' inks keep their hue on a dark page: Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Copilot read at full color and at least 4.5:1. - Images on a dark page draw at 90% brightness inside their faint rim. - Display math is centered in the column. - A table column of numbers aligns right unless its delimiter row sets an alignment. The head sits one row above the first row with a single rule under it, and columns have no rules between them. - Typst and TeX sources always show in the code face. - A change that lies wholly inside hidden markup, such as a link's new target, shows that markup, so its mark no longer sits on nothing. - The Changes segment counts what the toolbar counts: every change waiting in the window's notes and in notes changed while closed. - The change stamp stays in the margin when the Changes pane opens, compact ("CLAUDE · 1 of 3" over icon buttons) where the full stamp won't fit, so toggling the pane no longer reflows the note. Revert and Keep share one width, the counter always reads "1 of N", and the full stamp shows Next Change's keys (⌃⌘↓). Only the stamp at the caret, or under the pointer, shows its buttons. - Changes list rows show the text around the change, with Markdown markers taken out; Revert Session and Keep Session are buttons, Keep filled. - The rail's change label stays in the right margin, shortening the heading or dropping "Changes show here too" to fit, shows Next or Previous Change's keys, and stays hidden while the Changes pane is open. A note with no changes that fits on screen shows no rail track. - A folder window with no note open lists the notes waiting for review: marked changes, changes made while closed and notes git reports changed, each opening on Return or a click. Open CLAUDE.md is the default button, beside Set Up Agent Hooks… at the same width. - A tab with changes waiting shows the sidebar's writer badge with the count, in place of the dot. - Edit > Revert Session (⌃⌘⌫) and File > Earlier Versions… (⌥⌘Y) have shortcuts, and the title bar has a sidebar toggle. - A window opening on its own takes at least 1200 x 760 pt, or the whole screen when it is smaller. - The rail follows the system's scroll bar setting: when scroll bars show only while scrolling, it shows while the note scrolls or the pointer is on it. - The sidebar uses the system's sidebar material. - The selected tab no longer carries an orange bar; every tab shows its close button under the pointer. - Quick Open no longer dims the window behind it.
- An agent's edit marks one change per stretch of a line: word edits a few characters apart join, and a line more than 40% rewritten shows struck whole with the new line under it. - Earlier Versions names a hooked write's snapshot after its agent even when the hook reports after you decide the change, keeps a reverted change's save as "You (Revert)", and no longer adds an "Another app" copy of the version a reopened note already ends with. - Earlier Versions names the note in its heading, shows seconds when two versions share a minute, pins with a pin symbol, previews the whole difference with tinted lines and a +/− gutter, moves between versions with ↑ and ↓, and hides scroll bars with nothing to scroll. - The Welcome demo swaps a word in place ("revert" becomes "undo"), so one of its two changes is a true replacement. - The hook setup sheet is titled "Let Dewline see which agent made each edit", says it adds one local command (dewline notify) to PreToolUse and PostToolUse, that nothing leaves the Mac and where to remove it; it shows the backup's whole name, lines up with the text above it, and shortens long paths in the middle. - Settings > Agents gives each agent its own Set Up… or Remove, shows Codex as Not set up, Installed, needs trust, or Active, and says when each agent last named an edit. Set Up All Hooks… sits at the trailing edge. - Settings: rows of a disabled group dim with their switches, panes grow to the screen's height before they scroll, the four theme cards sit in one row under Light and Dark, every menu choice uses one pop-up style, Restore Defaults has a bezel, "Never" is set in the label face, and the font preview's sample heading reads "Public beta plan". - Settings is a standard grouped form with the system's switches, pop-up menus, steppers and buttons; each pane is as tall as its settings. - Find in Files puts its options on a second row so the field spans the sidebar, shows Regular Expression as ".*", adds a close button back to Files, and says what a search with no matches looked in, with a button that turns its options off. Snippets start a few words before a match far along its line, results sit on the sidebar's inset, and Replace All with an empty field asks to delete. - Quick Open no longer lists Open Recent's files or the Window menu's windows as commands, sets matched letters in semibold without an underline, gives notes a document symbol, and starts commands at the header's inset. - The sidebar puts a note's writer badge and git's letter together at the trailing edge; a closed folder shows a dot per writer. - A note git reports modified opens with its changes since the last commit marked, listed in Changes under Uncommitted; clicking its "M" in the sidebar opens that list. Keep only clears the marks: nothing is staged or committed. Changes an agent made while the note was closed, or marks left undecided, still come first. - The Export panel's Format menu lines up with the panel's own labels and fields. - An agent's write that adds list items no longer drops the bullet of the item after them. - Ticking a task box in an agent's change no longer shifts its row to the right. - A change's highlight leaves out the blanks at its ends and runs unbroken across inline code; code spans get rounded chips. - Inserted text is underlined with dots, so it no longer reads as a link, and each change gets one bar in the margin. - A long line in fenced code wraps one indent past its own indentation instead of at the block's left edge. - Spell check skips hyphenated words such as `at-least-once` and inline math, whose marks drew a red dot after the formula. - Table columns of numbers use tabular figures, and images on a dark page get a faint rim. - The Welcome demo's writer is named Example. - The sidebar shows git's state as one letter (M, A, R, D, U) in a fixed column, with the word in its tooltip, so the file under review keeps its name. A long name loses its middle, not its end. A closed folder shows a dot when a file under it changed since the last commit. - A folder window with no note open shows no tab. - Edit > Copy Relative Path (⌥⇧⌘C) copies the note's path under the folder; file rows and tabs have it in their menus. - Go > Reveal in Sidebar (⇧⌘J) selects the note's row and puts the keyboard on the sidebar. - Tabs for notes with the same name add the folder that tells them apart ("spec.md · api"). - A tab with changes waiting shows a dot in the writer's ink, and its tooltip says how many. - Edit > Keep Session (⌥⇧⌘↩) keeps every change of the session. - "No folder open" lines up with the sidebar's Outline header. - The hook setup sheet says in one sentence what hooks do and that agent edits still show without them, labeled Another app; it lists each settings file and its backup's name, and Show Details lists the JSON entries each file gains. - `dewline doctor --remove-hooks` takes Dewline's hooks out of each agent's settings, keeping a backup; `--agent` limits it, or `--install-hooks`, to one agent. Plain `dewline doctor` prints the entries `--install-hooks` would add. - Settings > Agents shows each agent's hook status with a symbol, with Set Up, Remove and Show File beside it. - Dewline no longer offers hook setup after the demo, only when a folder with agent files opens. Not Now applies to that folder; Don't offer again stops every offer. - Welcome.md leads with what Dewline does for agent edits and the demo link, says what Keep and Revert do, and uses curly quotes. The demo writes two changes, a replace and an insert. - A folder window with no note open says Dewline is watching the folder, shows whether agent hooks are on, and opens CLAUDE.md or README.md in one click. - Settings panes size to their content, and the selected theme's name keeps its weight. - Recent notes and folders in the launch window show how many changes wait for review. - With Open code files on, `.typ` files open as highlighted Typst. After Dewline saves a `.typ` or `.tex` file, or an agent's write lands in it, Dewline typesets it with the `typst`, `latexmk` or `tectonic` you have installed; the status bar shows errors with Go to Line, and error lines number in red. File > Export writes the PDF. Dewline bundles no compiler. - A scan of closed files also covers `.typ` and `.tex`, so an agent's write to one while it was closed opens marked. - `dewline doctor` lists `latexmk` and `tectonic`. - latexmk runs each LaTeX engine with shell escape off and TeX refusing absolute and parent-folder paths, so a `.tex` file can't run commands or pull outside files into its PDF. A `% !TEX root` outside the folder stops the typeset with an error. - typst, tectonic and latexmk run in a sandbox that reads only the folder, system and TeX folders, so a symlink in a cloned repo can't pull a file such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` into the PDF; only typst and tectonic reach the network. Inside it they run only toolchain programs and can't open other apps. latexmk refuses file names other than letters, digits, space, dot, dash and underscore, skips bibtex, biber and makeindex, and runs lualatex with `--safer --nosocket`. - A change's stamp reads "1 of 3" and its buttons stay Keep and Revert at a fixed width, turning into icons where the margin is narrow. Holding Option turns them into Keep All and Revert All, and their tooltips say what each does. - The Changes list groups changes by writer session, closed notes included, under a heading with Keep Session and Revert Session. Its bylines survive a relaunch and its rows are 24 pt. - Status bar problems show a red octagon, and their actions are buttons. A typeset error inside a marked change says whose change it is and offers Revert Change. - The rail's on-screen bracket has a light fill, and the first change ever to land is labeled on the rail, "Changes show here too". - README and the site say Dewline is free to start. Decision 0011 replaces 0001's pricing promise: every feature in the app is free for everyone, and paid plans cover only services that run on our servers.

- Math, Mermaid diagrams and images are sharp on Retina screens. Math and diagrams are drawn as vector outlines at the screen's own scale, and redraw when a window moves between screens. - Math and diagram labels use the same text color as the note, and diagram lines and borders follow the theme, so they no longer look faded next to the text. - Images keep their own color profile.

First launch shows one sheet, and a note ignored by git no longer opens unmarked after an agent writes to it.
- First launch offers to install agent hooks and no longer stacks the default-app sheet on Welcome; Settings > General still sets the default app. (#181) - Dewline offers to install agent hooks once for each folder holding `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.codex`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. In 0.4.0 the first offer was the only one, so a later agent folder was never offered. (#181) - Settings > Agents shows hooks as set up right after Set Up finishes. (#181) - Command-T in a window with no folder asks for one, like Command-N; Cancel opens no tab. (#181) - An agent write to a note that `.gitignore` ignores, such as `CLAUDE.local.md`, is marked again. This corrects 0.4.0, which skipped ignored notes. The scan lists tracked notes first, then ignored ones, newest first, within the 10,000-note cap. (#183) - A scan of closed notes also covers `.mdx` and `.qmd` files and the `.agents`, `.codex`, `.kiro`, `.ruler`, `.specify` and `.windsurf` folders. (#183) - Marks are kept on every landing of an outside change, including one that lands into unsaved typing or mid-conflict. (#183) - A save that waits more than 5 seconds on another app, such as a sync client, fails and retries, so quitting no longer hangs behind it. (#183) - README and the site state iCloud and iPhone behavior as designed: the device test in `docs/sync.md` has not been run. The README no longer quotes the 0.1.0 performance run. (#182)

Fewer settings and no Documents folder made for you, new notes go where you picked, and agent edits from Cursor and shell commands are named more accurately. Keeping an iCloud version no longer throws the other one away.
- Keep This Version on an iCloud conflict first saves the other version into the note's snapshots, so File > Earlier Versions can restore it. If that save fails, or the note keeps no snapshots, the other version stays unresolved with iCloud. (#178) - Closing a note in the middle of a conflict keeps the conflict as a marked change over the other version; Revert puts yours back. A Keep, or a change that lands over unsaved typing, also keeps its marks across close. This corrects the 0.3.0 note that conflict cards were not kept. (#178) - Settings drops Motion, Heading style, Smart Punctuation, Open notes in, When Dewline opens and New notes go in. Smart Punctuation stays in the Edit menu and the palette. (#173) - First launch no longer writes `~/Documents/Dewline`. Welcome opens in a window with no folder, and a note anywhere in `~/Library` opens without scanning it. (#173) - Command-N, New Folder and New Window with no folder window ask for a folder and remember it; Settings > General shows it as New notes go in once set, and Restore Defaults clears it. If the folder is gone, you are asked again, and Cancel makes nothing. Command-T in a window with no folder leaves the note untitled until you save it. (#173, #174, #177) - Export opens in the note's folder. Quick Open and Find in Files list gitignored notes while Show files .gitignore hides is on. (#173) - Renaming or moving a note no longer freezes the window while links to it are rewritten, and File > Rename can be undone. (#177) - Closing a note that another app deleted after a refused save shows the save sheet. (#177) - Git status: files whose only change is the executable bit are not listed when `core.fileMode` is off; CRLF files are not listed under `core.autocrlf`; Git LFS files compare against their pointer. SHA-256 repositories show no status. (#172) - A Cursor edit to a closed note is named Cursor instead of Another app. The shell-command mark applies only to notes under the folder the Bash command ran in. (#179) - Dewline offers to install agent hooks once at first launch and when you open a folder holding `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.codex`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. `dewline doctor` also reads that folder's project hook files and reports "hooks off" when `disableAllHooks` is set. (#179) - Pasting or dropping text into a CRLF note inserts CRLF. (#179) - A scan of closed notes skips what `.gitignore` ignores. Past 10,000 notes it keeps the most recently modified. (#178) - Release builds no longer run a performance check. (#170)

iCloud conflicts ask which version stays, files you open from Finder get the right folder, Revert works after you type around a change, and agent edits from shell commands and Cursor are marked.
- When iCloud keeps two versions of a note, a sheet names the other version's device and time and asks which stays. Use the Other Version lands as a marked change that Revert undoes. Saves now go through file coordination, so iCloud sees them. Welcome and the docs have a new Sync and mobile page. (#146, #165) - A file opened from Finder, `dewline open` or Open Recent opens in the window whose folder holds it, else on its git root, else on its parent folder. Command-N there writes in that window's folder. The open tabs are saved as you change them, so a crash reopens them. Many tabs on one folder share one watch and one scan. (#147) - A note in your home folder opens as a single-file window instead of scanning all of home and `~/Library`. Closing or quitting after another app deletes a note you have typed in shows the save sheet. Settings > General and a first-launch sheet offer to make Dewline the default app, and `.mdc`, `.mdx` and `.qmd` files open from File > Open and Open With. Code file types leave Open With. (#164) - A change from a Claude Code shell command is marked "During Claude Code's shell command" instead of Another app. Setup installs Cursor hooks, so Cursor's file edits carry its name; Settings shows Codex as Needs trust until you trust it. (#149) - Revert works after you type next to a change and keeps your typing. When you typed inside the change, the stamp says so. (#155) - The sidebar, Quick Open, Find in Files and [[ completion follow .gitignore the way git does: nested files, `.git/info/exclude`, your global ignore file, and negations. `[[` completion lists notes without freezing the window. (#153, #150, #166) - Git status shows a staged rename with edits as Renamed, and a rename into a subfolder as Renamed. (#150) - Exported HTML, PDF and the preview page color code blocks. (#150) - Source mode shows line numbers. The scroller rail ticks H1, H2 and H3. Wide Mermaid flowcharts fold into bands so labels stay readable, and inline code in a wrapped table column no longer breaks at a slash. (#151) - A new note takes its name from its first line when you leave it or close it, Command-T notes too, and an empty Untitled note you never typed in is removed when you close it. File > Share is the system share menu. (#156) - Return in a CRLF note inserts CRLF. Links to a note follow it when you rename it from File > Rename, drag it in the sidebar, or move or rename its folder. Replace All and link rewrites in closed notes show as yours, not Another app. (#166) - Only Markdown files list as changed while a note is closed; a hooked write to a `.env` or other file no longer does. Notes in `.claude`, `.cursor` and `.github` get closed-note changes, and `.mdc` files count as Markdown. Marks for undecided changes survive a crash. (#165) - Security fixes: a dangling symlink as the last part of a note path is refused, so a save cannot follow it to `~/.ssh`; moving a symlinked folder no longer rewrites the files it points to; and a Rust panic in any of twenty core calls shows an error or an empty result instead of crashing the app. (#157, #158, #168)

Notes save themselves, undecided changes survive closing, and export gains seven more formats; live collaboration, the agent chat panel, Follow Changes, the Preview pane and the font catalog are gone.
- Closing a tab, quitting, sleeping the Mac or switching apps saves your notes with no save sheet. Typing without a pause saves within 10 seconds. When a save is refused, the status bar says why and offers Save Now, and the text is kept as a draft that reopening the note offers to restore. Symlinked notes save in place. - Changes you have not decided on survive closing a tab and quitting, and reopening shows them at the same lines. A write to a closed note by another app, or while Dewline was quit, shows up as marked changes when you open it, and the sidebar badges the note with the writer and the count. Reading a note no longer credits an agent for someone else's later write. - A new look: the window, toolbar, tab strip and sidebar are redrawn, with a new palette, Seravek for text and SF Mono for code. The scroller rail shows headings and waiting changes, each change is reviewed at the change, and the sidebar shows each file's git status. - Tab and Shift-Tab move between table cells, and Tab in the last cell adds a row. Format > Insert Row and Insert Column edit a table. View > Zoom In, Zoom Out and Actual Size (Command-+, Command-- and Command-0) resize the text. Pasted JPEG, GIF, WebP and PNG images keep their original bytes. Edit > Copy as Markdown and Copy as HTML, and pasting from a web page or Mail gives Markdown. - Export to plain text, RTF, OpenDocument, EPUB, LaTeX, PNG and portable Markdown, besides PDF, Word and HTML. Portable Markdown turns wikilinks into relative links and copies images beside the file. - Code blocks highlight 50 languages, in Quick Look too. Hovering a block shows its language and a Copy button. Settings > Editor has Open code files, off by default: with it on, code files open in the editor as code, with the same highlighting, line numbers and no Markdown rendering. - Find in Files takes regular expressions, a `path:` filter and a Replace field. Replace All asks first, counts what it changed, and is one undo in an open note. - View > Sidebar Outline swaps the tree for the note's headings. Typing [[ lists the folder's notes. Renaming a note in the sidebar rewrites the links to it across the folder, and undo points them back. View > Backlinks lists the notes that link to the open note and opens each one at its link. - The `.claude`, `.cursor` and `.github` folders and `.mdc` files show in the tree, Quick Open and Find in Files. `dewline open <folder>` opens a folder in its window, and File > Open Recent lists recent folders and notes. - Settings has four panes: General, Editor, Appearance and Agents. There are four themes: Tidewater and Onionskin for light, Nightwatch and Carbon for dark, and a retired theme becomes the nearest of these. Body, headings and code take any font on your Mac. Link previews stay off until you turn them on in Settings > Editor. - File > Capture is the one place in the app that adds a line to your inbox. The Service, the App Intent, `dewline capture` and MCP work as before, and Settings > General holds the inbox path. - Agent setup skips agents you have not installed and says when Codex needs to trust Dewline's hooks. Edits made with curly quotes or in CRLF files are matched, so more agent edits carry the agent's name, and a failed edit no longer delays the next change. A nightly test runs Claude Code and Codex against these checks. - Removed: live collaboration is off for now, so Share, Join Shared Note and `dewline://join` are not in this build. The agent chat panel, Follow Changes, the Preview pane, the font catalog and installable fonts, the extra theme pack, and the daily note, Dock capture and capture shortcut are gone. - Security fixes in the URL scheme and in LaTeX and EPUB export.

A new look and a calmer window, a live preview, and a panel for your own coding agent.
- The window title names the open note and its folder. The sidebar starts at your folder's name, with + for a new note, and a native toolbar replaces the old top bar. - Open the preview to see the note rendered on the right while you edit its Markdown on the left. - Chat with your own coding agent beside the note. Dewline talks to it over the Agent Client Protocol, and its edits arrive marked, with Keep and Revert. Dewline ships no model and needs no account. - Links are quieter. A link on its own line shows a preview card, and hovering a link shows one; Settings turns previews off. - Which instruction files your agents read in a folder now shows in the status bar. - Reopening a note brings you back to the same place in it. - Sharing a note works again: the share popover opens, and join requests show in the status bar with Approve and Deny. - `dewline export --to pdf` writes the PDF again. - A new app icon, and headings use the system font by default.

The first public build. Dewline is a native Markdown editor for Mac: it opens the .md files you already keep, in place, and renders them as you write. Links, embeds, math, diagrams, export and live collaboration are built in, and every save changes only what you edited. No account and no telemetry.
- Open any Markdown file and edit it in place. Syntax hides until the caret reaches it; tables, task boxes, footnotes, callouts and highlighted code render in the page, and math and Mermaid diagrams are drawn natively. Wikilinks, embeds and #tags follow Obsidian's syntax. - Saves change only the bytes you edited, and never overwrite a newer version on disk. File > Snapshots restores an earlier version of the file. Export to HTML, PDF or DOCX, and preview .md files in Finder with Quick Look. - Open a folder or an Obsidian vault in place. A sidebar for the folder and your agent files, tabs, Quick Open (Shift-Command-O), find in files (Shift-Command-F) and one palette for files, commands and settings (Shift-Command-P). - Edit a file live with someone by invite link, peer to peer. - Six themes plus a pack of four, installable fonts, Vim mode, a Source view, and focus and typewriter modes. - When git, a sync app, a script or a coding agent changes the open file, Dewline marks each change, and names the agent when its hooks report it. Keep or revert each one, or all at once; Dewline snapshots the file first. - `dewline open file.md:12 --wait` works as `$EDITOR`, `dewline notify` lets agent hooks name their edits, and `dewline mcp` serves a folder's notes to an agent.
